A mutex, short for mutual exclusion, is a synchronization primitive used in concurrent programming. Its main purpose is to prevent multiple threads from accessing a shared resource simultaneously.

So, the first thing it protects against is race conditions. Race conditions occur when two or more threads access shared data and try to change it at the same time, leading to inconsistent or corrupted data. By ensuring that only one thread can access the resource at a time, the mutex prevents this.
